column1: # src/dis.s — decode cases. The expectations here are written by hand from the
# encodings in docs/encodings.md and the x86 branch rules (target = site +
# length + displacement), NOT produced by running the decoder. A decoder tested
# against its own output proves nothing.
# The expected column is the WHOLE line dis must print, so the site it echoes,
# its spelling, and the mnemonic are all pinned. `refuse` means: exit non-zero
# and not one byte on stdout.
# field 1 is the input as hex; `-` means an empty input.
# --- the sixteen jcc rel8 names, 0x70..0x7f, displacement 0, target 2 --------
# eb 04 -> 0 + 2 + 4 = 6, and 6 < 7 so it is a byte in the input
# 0X0 is the same offset as 0x0, and the output is always lowercase and
# unpadded, so the site is echoed canonically rather than copied.
# the same bytes with a 4-byte input: the 0F form needs six, so the bounds rule
# fires first -- trunc, not form. The order of the checks is part of the answer.
